paper.title: Combinatorial Multi-Armed Bandits with Filtered Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: CMAB with filtered semibandit feedback (general mean estimator satisfying Assumption 3)
unmapped: Filtered semibandit feedback: the learner observes, for each played base arm, a filtered observation Y drawn from a filtering distribution conditioned on the true outcome X and on the played super arm S_t, rather than X itself
Expected reward function satisfies monotonicity and bounded smoothness with a strictly increasing function f (Chen et al. 2013)
The learner knows constants c, v of the mean-estimator concentration inequality (Assumption 3) and has an exact combinatorial optimisation oracle

settings.name_in_paper: Semibandit Feedback with Heavy Tails (CMAB without filtering)
unmapped: Expected reward function satisfies monotonicity and bounded smoothness with a strictly increasing function f (Chen et al. 2013)
settings.definition_quote:

unmapped: Underlying outcomes are Poisson(mu_i) and are observed only through binomial filtering Y ~ Bin(X, gamma_{i,S_t}) with detection probabilities depending on the played super arm
The learner knows the detection probabilities gamma_{i,S}, a lower bound gamma_min on them, and an upper bound mu_max on the Poisson means
Expected reward function satisfies monotonicity and bounded smoothness with a strictly increasing function f
settings.definition_quote: one possible filtering framework is the Binomial filtering of count data, i.e. where if in round $t$ $X_{i,T_{i,t}}$ is a draw from $\nu_i$ and $S_t$ is the combination of arms selected then the filtering distribution for arm $i$, $\tilde{\nu}_i(X_{i,T_{i,t}},S_t)$ is $Bin(X_{i,T_{i,t}},\gamma_{i,S_t})$. ... with the additional assumption that for some $\gamma_{min}>0$ we have $\gamma_{i,S}>\gamma_{min}$ for all $i$ and $S \in \mathcal{S}$.

algorithms.name: Robust-F-CUCB with filtered truncated empirical mean

symbols.c_conc: constant c in the estimator concentration Assumption 3
symbols.v_conc: constant v in the estimator concentration Assumption 3
symbols.finv_Delta_min: f^{-1}(Delta_min), inverse of the bounded smoothness function at the minimum super-arm gap

conditions: Assumption 1 (monotonicity) and Assumption 2 (bounded smoothness with function f)
mean estimator satisfies Assumption 3 for all arms under the filtering distributions
Delta_min, Delta_max are gaps between super arms' expected rewards
tuning: UCB index hat mu + v^{1/(1+eps)} (c ln t^3 / T_i)^{eps/(1+eps)}
results.notes: Regret defined as n*opt - E sum r_mu(S_t): pseudo-regret. K = k number of base arms. Exact combinatorial oracle assumed; compute not stated.

symbols.finv_Delta_min: f^{-1}(Delta_min), inverse of the bounded smoothness function at the minimum super-arm gap

source.quote:
Let $\epsilon \in (0,1]$ and $u > 0$. Let the reward distributions $
u_1,...,
u_k$ satisfy $\mathds{E}_{X \sim 
u_i}|X_i|^{1+\epsilon} \leq u$ ... Then the regret of the Robust-F-CUCB algorithm used with the truncated empirical mean estimator defined in (ef{TruncatedEmpiricalMean}) satisfies Reg <= (12(4u)^{1/eps}(2/f^{-1}(Delta_min))^{(1+eps)/eps} ln n + pi^2/3 + 1) k Delta_max.

results.notes: Raw (1+eps) moment bound u maps to u_mom.

symbols.mu_max: known upper bound on the Poisson means
symbols.finv_Delta_min: f^{-1}(Delta_min), inverse of the bounded smoothness function at the minimum super-arm gap

conditions: underlying distributions Poisson with mu_i <= mu_max
tuning: eps = 1, c = u_max = mu_max^2 + mu_max, v = (2/gamma_min + sqrt(2/gamma_min) + 1/3)^2
results.notes: Lemma 3's estimator uses ln(1/delta) in the truncation, which the algorithm instantiates with t^{-3}; the proposition relies on this. Discussion notes O(k^3 ln n) for the search application with f(Lambda)=k Lambda (informal, not recorded).
